title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The UK government responds to the 2020 Committee report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards, affirming its commitment to create clear rules that protect citizens and promote trustworthy AI. It outlines plans to improve transparency, accountability, and regulation while investing in research and partnerships to ensure AI systems support public values and interests.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is setting out how it will monitor and control the use of artificial intelligence in qualification assessments, aiming to keep tests fair, accurate, and trustworthy. The policy was issued after a joint request from the Secretaries of State for Education, Science, Innovation and Technology, and Business and Trade to safeguard the integrity of the qualifications sector.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how copyright-protected content is used to train and develop AI systems, evaluating the legal, economic, and ethical effects of that practice. It offers recommendations to balance creators’ rights with the benefits and opportunities that AI brings.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The government has issued a response to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report on artificial intelligence, titled “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency.” In it, officials outline their stance on the committee’s findings and propose specific measures to strengthen AI regulation, research, and workforce development in the UK.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document outlines the purpose, scope, and responsibilities of a committee tasked with reviewing how artificial intelligence intersects with public standards. It also provides frequently asked questions to guide stakeholders in understanding the committee’s role and the review process.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: The CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee on the governance of artificial intelligence. This submission outlines the organization’s perspectives and recommendations on how AI should be regulated and ethically managed.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The policy explains how artificial intelligence will change the rules for medical products, addressing new challenges and opportunities. It focuses on applying the AI White Paper principles to ensure safety, effectiveness, and ethical use in healthcare.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy outlines how the organisation plans to become the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential AI-driven defence entity for its size. It focuses on developing advanced AI capabilities, fostering collaboration, and ensuring responsible use to maintain strategic advantage and credibility.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan outlines how the Department for Transport will collaborate with the transport sector to harness AI opportunities while addressing potential risks. It details strategies, partnerships, and safeguards to ensure safe and effective AI integration in transport services.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: This report outlines how copyright‑protected materials are used in training and developing AI systems under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It tracks progress, highlights challenges, and offers recommendations for balancing AI innovation with copyright protection.
